## Conclusion

**Yes.** The strongest direct evidence is the Chinese phase III BEYOND randomized trial: adding bevacizumab to first-line carboplatin–paclitaxel improved progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and overall survival (OS) versus chemotherapy alone in advanced or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC. A separate Chinese real-world cohort also found longer PFS with first-line bevacizumab-containing pemetrexed–platinum therapy, although its observational design limits causal interpretation.

## Evidence

| Study | Population and treatment | Efficacy | Safety and limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BEYOND, phase III randomized, double-blind trial** (PMID **26014294**; DOI **10.1200/JCO.2014.59.4424**) | 276 Chinese patients randomized 1:1 (138/arm) with locally advanced, metastatic, or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC. Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles, with bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death, versus placebo plus the same chemotherapy. | Median PFS **9.2 vs 6.5 months**; HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.29–0.54; P<0.001). ORR **54% vs 26%**. Median OS **24.3 vs 17.7 months**; HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.50–0.93; P=0.0154). | The report describes the regimen as well tolerated, with safety similar to previous bevacizumab–chemotherapy studies and no new safety signals. The abstract does not provide adverse-event rates or grade-specific toxicity. The trial provides direct randomized evidence in Chinese patients, but includes 276 participants and does not by itself establish safety for every clinical subgroup. |
| **Chinese retrospective propensity-score-matched cohort** (PMID **31814679**) | 415 patients receiving first-line pemetrexed–platinum: 106 received bevacizumab (7.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks) and 309 did not; matching yielded 105 pairs. | Median PFS in the overall cohort: **9.8 vs 7.8 months** (P=0.006); in matched pairs: **9.8 vs 6.6 months** (P<0.001). PFS was **12.3 months** with pemetrexed–bevacizumab maintenance, **8.6 months** with pemetrexed-only maintenance, and **4.8 months** when maintenance was interrupted (P<0.001). The available abstract does not report ORR or OS. | Retrospective treatment selection leaves potential residual confounding despite matching; outcomes may also reflect differences in maintenance treatment. The available report excerpt does not provide detailed adverse-event rates. |
| **Additional Chinese real-world cohort identified** (PMID **33209891**) | Single-center review of **194** patients with non-squamous NSCLC treated with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy in first-, second-, or later-line settings. | The retrieved search record identifies the study but does not provide numerical response, PFS, or OS results, so it cannot independently quantify benefit here. | Mixed treatment lines and retrospective single-center design limit comparison with first-line randomized evidence; detailed safety results were not available in the retrieved record. |

**Overall interpretation:** BEYOND establishes a clinically meaningful benefit for bevacizumab added to carboplatin–paclitaxel in the studied Chinese population. The pemetrexed–platinum cohort is directionally consistent for PFS, but is not randomized. The available evidence supports efficacy; detailed, regimen-specific toxicity rates are not available in the retrieved reports.

**Yes.** In the Chinese phase III BEYOND randomized trial, 276 patients with advanced or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC received carboplatin–paclitaxel with either bevacizumab or placebo. Adding bevacizumab improved:

- **Median progression-free survival:** 9.2 vs 6.5 months (HR 0.40; 95% CI 0.29–0.54; P<0.001)
- **Objective response rate:** 54% vs 26%
- **Median overall survival:** 24.3 vs 17.7 months (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.50–0.93; P=0.0154)

A Chinese retrospective cohort also reported longer PFS with bevacizumab plus pemetrexed–platinum, though its nonrandomized design means confounding is possible (PMID: 31814679). The randomized trial reported the regimen was well tolerated, but the retrieved evidence did not provide detailed adverse-event rates. These results support efficacy in the studied population; individual suitability depends on clinical factors.

**Key evidence:** BEYOND trial, PMID: 26014294; observational cohort, PMID: 31814679.
